Each discipline section holds Brandt-workbook / Air-Force-manual / internet OUTPUTS that the framework's computed results are compared AGAINST -- these are NOT toolbox inputs (see examples/F16A/*_L*.json for inputs). _source: Brandt-F16-A.xls geometry values + VnV/BrandtF16A/readme_aero.md (Brandt aero, cell refs) + T.O. 1F-16A-1 (AF-manual aero) + cited internet sources (aerodynamics).
_note_columns: Aerodynamics comparison columns are Brandt + AF-Manual (T.O. 1F-16A-1) + internet (no F16Baseline column). Read as the comparison target by examples/F16A/geometry_brandt_comparison.m and aerodynamics_brandt_comparison.m; never backfill a unit-test expected value from this file.

geometry._comment: F-16A Block 10/15 Brandt-workbook ground-truth geometry values, for examples/F16A/geometry_brandt_comparison.m to check computed L1 / L2 / L3 toolbox output against. Geometry is an L1/L2/L3 discipline: the 2026-07-22 'L3 eliminated and merged into L2' decision (src/disciplines/geometry/GeomL2.md's dated note) was REVERSED on 2026-07-24, and Phase 2 (2026-07-25) promotes GeomL3 to the full L3 geometry tier consumed by L3 geometry + aero + weights — so the comparison report gains an L3 column, a T.O. 1F-16A-1 second-source column, and a divergence-annotation column (spec: examples/F16A/F16GeomL3.md §G.1). These are NOT toolbox inputs: inputs live in the unified per-level files examples/F16A/f16a_L{1,2,3}.json (.geometry blocks read by F16GeomL1/L2/L3); the former examples/F16A/geometry_L*.json files no longer exist. Everything here is a Brandt Geom-tab OUTPUT / validation figure (plus, where noted, a Brandt Main-tab GIVEN input or a T.O./USAF second source) to compare computed results against. NEVER backfill a unit-test 'expected' value from anything in this file — several rows are deliberate BY-DESIGN divergences where a large %Diff is the correct answer.
geometry._source: VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/Brandt-F16-A.xls (Geom sheet unless noted); VnV/BrandtF16A/readme_geom.md; VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/cell-map.md; VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md; T.O. 1F-16A-1 and the USAF 3-view for the to_1f16a1 second-source block. Cell values re-confirmed live via MATLAB readcell 2026-07-21 during this JSON-authoring phase (full-precision reads shown where they refine the readme's rounded figures); the Main-tab cells and Geom!A20/B20/A21/B21/H47 were re-read live over Excel COM 2026-07-25 during the Phase-2 scribe pass. Workbook integrity: the working-tree Brandt-F16-A.xls was diffed against git HEAD across all seven cited tabs (Main, Geom, Aero, Wt, Engn(s), Consts, Miss) with readmatrix on 2026-07-25 — every numeric cell identical, so every cell citation here is safe (todo.md 2026-07-25 Phase 2 §14).

fuselage_S_wet.high_fi_source: Geom!D23 — trapezoidal frame-integration of per-frame perimeters. readme_geom.md Section 4.1. RESOLVED per VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md Finding 3 (2026-07-21 user decision): fuselage S_wet ground truth is Geom!B3 (low-fi) / Geom!D23 (high-fi) — NOT Geom!A3/A4, which are label cells (A3='Fuselage', A4='Exposed Engine Nacelles'), not a second fuselage-S_wet pair.

lifting_surface_S_wet_ft2._source: Geom!A11:C17 (full labeled table, header 'Exposed Lifting Surface Swet') / B14:B17 (value column) — confirmed live exact match, VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md Finding 2.

pitch_control_HT.label: Exposed Pitch Trim Surface Wetted Area

lifting_surface_exposed_areas._source: Geom!A5:I10 — 'Exposed Lifting Surf Geometry' table (header rows 5-6: Xexposed, Root Chord, Tip Chord, Span, Root Chord (exposed), Half Span (exposed), Exposed S; data rows 7-10 = Wing/Pitch Control Surface/Strake/Vertical Tail). Range confirmed live exact match, VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md Finding 1. Full row re-read live via MATLAB readcell 2026-07-21 (Scribe's companion docs, readme_geom.md Section 4.5's 'Surface parameters' table, only reproduced a partial subset of these columns for the cosine cross-section formula — this block carries the complete raw table).

whole_aircraft_S_wet_ft2.raw_buggy_source: Geom!B19 — KNOWN EXCEL BUG: strake wetted area is double-counted. Workbook formula Geom!B19 = D23+B4+B14+B15+B16+B17+K21 includes both B15 (strake S_wet) and K21 (strake-chine wetted-area term, also strake S_wet). readme_geom.md top-of-file note + Section 6.2. This is a documented audit exception, not a silent deviation.
whole_aircraft_S_wet_ft2.corrected_source: readme_geom.md Section 6.2 — corrected total with the double-counted strake term removed. This is the value the comparison report should target for whole-aircraft S_wet; up to 2% error (vs. the usual 1% target used elsewhere in readme_geom.md) is the documented audit exception, because the workbook formula itself is known-bad, not because of any modeling looseness.
whole_aircraft_S_wet_ft2.strake_chine_term_source: Geom!K21 — the strake-chine wetted-area term responsible for the B19 double-count. GroundTruth/cell-map.md.

nacelle._note: No nacelle component exists in the framework's get_S_wet aggregation at any level (wing + HT + VT + fuselage + duct only; the duct term sits in GeomL2 and, as of Phase 2, GeomL3). S_wet_ft2=41.515 is therefore recorded as a Brandt figure for a DIFFERENT quantity than the framework's duct term — the comparison-report duct row (computed 155.5664 ft2, an inlet-to-exit frustum) is annotated 'definitional', not an agreement check. diameter_ft=3.537 IS a genuine agreement check: the framework uses Brandt's own D=sqrt(T_AB_SLS/1900) formula, and as of Phase 2/3a the thrust reaches geometry by dependency injection from the propulsion object (prop.T_SL) rather than a hardcoded copy, so this row doubles as the positive control that the DI reproduces the previously-frozen value. Engine-side twin of this block: .propulsion.nacelle (same numbers, one shared truth).
nacelle.S_wet_source: Geom!B4 — 'Exposed Engine Nacelles' (Geom!C4 label: 'Full Cylinder approximation'). readme_geom.md Section 4.4 — cell formula itself could not be confirmed from the binary .xls; this GT value is used as-is.
nacelle.diameter_source: Engn(s) tab: D_engine = sqrt(T_AB_SLS_lb / 1900) = sqrt(23770/1900). readme_geom.md Section 3; GroundTruth/cell-map.md 'Engn(s)' section (Engn!D_nac).
nacelle.length_source: Engn(s) tab: L_engine = 4.5 * D_engine. readme_geom.md Section 3; GroundTruth/cell-map.md 'Engn(s)' section (Engn!L_nac).

aircraft_length_ft.source: Geom!B21 ('Total Aircraft Length:' label, Geom!A21). Confirmed live 2026-07-21 (rounded 48.3039) and re-read live over Excel COM 2026-07-25 at full precision. readme_geom.md Section 8, Table 2 cites the rounded figure 48.304 ft.
aircraft_length_ft._formula: Geom!B21 = MAX(L38:L44,L46:L121,L123:L141,L152,...,L169) — a maximum over Brandt's component x-station columns, i.e. the aft-most modelled station of HIS OWN component layout.
aircraft_length_ft._note: NOT the same quantity as the framework's overall_length_ft input (47.65 ft, published F-16A airframe length 47 ft 7.75 in). Brandt's figure is an EXTENT of his layout; the framework's is a SPEC dimension. The -1.35% gap is definitional, not an error in either number, so the comparison-report row must be annotated 'definitional' (F16GeomL3.md §G.1 row 41 / §E). It also matches neither the commonly-quoted 49 ft 5 in (~49.42 ft, with pitot boom) figure. Cross-reference the T.O./published second source in to_1f16a1.overall_length_ft below, whose provenance is a standing OPEN item (todo.md 2026-07-25 Phase 2 §6).

Amax_ft2.source: Geom!B20 ('Total Aircraft Amax:' label, Geom!A20) = Geom!H47 (same value per GroundTruth/cell-map.md) — both cells confirmed live 2026-07-21 to read 25.1106 ft2, not a conflict (B20's formula is literally '=H47'); re-read live over Excel COM 2026-07-25 at full precision.
Amax_ft2._formula: Geom!H47 = MAX(H26:H45) - Main!B28*3.141579*C475^2/5 — i.e. a whole-aircraft AREA-RULED maximum cross-section, NET of engine flow-through: raw max 32.971053 ft2 minus N_eng*pi*D_nac^2/5 = 7.8605 ft2. (NB Brandt hardcodes pi as 3.141579.)
Amax_ft2.raw_max_source: Geom!H47's MAX(H26:H45) term before the engine deduction: 25.110556 + pi*3.537^2/5 = 32.971053 ft2. Recorded live-consistent 2026-07-25 (F16GeomL3.md §D; todo.md 2026-07-25 Phase 2 §5).
Amax_ft2._note_open_item: WHICH of these is the right comparison target is an OPEN item (todo.md 2026-07-25 Phase 2 §5): Brandt deducts pi*D^2/5 while readme_geom.md §4.5 states the same nacelle's OWN cross-section as pi*D^2/4 = 9.826 ft2, with no stated justification for removing only 80% of the duct area. Until that is resolved 'value' (25.11055621, Brandt's own published figure) stays the primary target and raw_max_ft2 is recorded alongside it — no choice has been made here.
Amax_ft2._note: DIFFERENT quantity from the framework's Amax. Phase 2 makes Amax a geometry Dependent = (pi/4)*W_max_fuselage*H_max_fuselage = 27.4889 ft2, the maximum cross-section of the equivalent elliptical-section fuselage the rest of the model already assumes (D_fus=(W+H)/2 feeding Roskam Eq. 12.3) — an envelope figure with no nacelle/strake/area-ruling content. +9.47% vs 25.110556, -16.6% vs the raw 32.971053. Comparison row annotated 'definitional' (F16GeomL3.md §G.1 row 40 / §D). The framework formula has NO pinnable equation number in any reference in this repo and is documented as a standard elliptical-cross-section identity (todo.md 2026-07-25 Phase 2 §4, OPEN) — do not invent one. This row previously read 'NOT MODELED' in the comparison report while F16AeroL3 consumed 25.110556 as a frozen input; Phase 2c removes that contradiction.

inputs_on_Main_tab._note: Brandt Main-tab GIVEN inputs (his own spec sheet), recorded as COMPARISON REFERENCES for the report's BY-DESIGN divergence rows and for citation audit — not Brandt outputs, and not framework targets in the agreement sense. Mirrors the .weights.inputs_on_Wt_tab block's role. All cells read live over Excel COM 2026-07-25 (values and row labels verbatim). CITATION MAP, corrected repo-wide 2026-07-25 (examples/F16A/F16GeomL3.md §F is authoritative): row 18 = 'S, sq ft', row 19 = 'Aspect Ratio', row 20 = 'Taper Ratio', row 21 = 'Sweep, deg', row 22 = 'NACA 4-digit', row 24 = 'Y Location' (B24/C24 EMPTY, H24=0), row 27 = 'TE Sweep'. The repo previously cited row 21 for taper, row 20 for sweep and row 24 for t/c; zero computed values change from the correction.
inputs_on_Main_tab._columns: B = wing, C = pitch control (HT), H = vertical surface (VT)

wing._note: Main!B27 TE sweep is a live formula '=Geom!N45'; the framework's GeometryBase.convert_sweep(40,3,0.2275,1.0) reproduces it as -0.0002 deg — an independent positive control for the mirrored 4/AR sweep identity.

pitch_control_HT._note: Main!C19 AR=3.0 is a COMPARISON REFERENCE ONLY, not a framework input: per Decision 1 (user, 2026-07-25) L3 fixes the HT planform from S_ht=108 plus the physical span 18.5 ft, making AR_ht DERIVED = 3.1690 (+5.63% vs this cell) — see to_1f16a1.HT_span_ft. Brandt's AR 3.0 with S 108 implies span sqrt(AR*S)=18.0 ft, which is the span_full_ft in lifting_surface_exposed_areas.pitch_control_HT. Main!C27 TE sweep is a live formula '=Geom!N122'.

vertical_tail._note: Main!H21 sweep=40 is the Brandt side of an INTENTIONAL divergence: L3 geometry uses the physical T.O. 47.5 deg (todo.md 2026-07-24 GeomL3 §2). Main!H27 TE sweep is a BARE LITERAL 0, unlike the wing/HT live formulas, and contradicts Brandt's OWN VT planform (S=60, AR=1.6, lambda=0.5, LE=40 imply TE sweep 22.9008 deg — exactly what the framework's single-panel convert_sweep_panel returns). Recorded so nobody 'corrects' the framework's 22.90 deg back to 0 (todo.md 2026-07-25 Phase 2 §9, informational).

fuselage._note: Main!B32 length 46.5 is the Brandt side of an INTENTIONAL divergence: L3 geometry uses the physical T.O. 47.5 ft (todo.md 2026-07-24 GeomL3 §3); L2 uses 46.5. C32/D32 are unchanged at both levels.

n_engines._note: Used by the Geom!H47 Amax engine-flow-through deduction above.

to_1f16a1._note: SECOND-SOURCE column for the comparison report (T.O. 1F-16A-1 / USAF 3-view), mirroring the .aerodynamics.af_manual block's role. These are the physical/T.O. figures GeomL3 uses where they differ from Brandt — so they are the SAME numbers the f16a_L3.json .geometry inputs carry (one shared truth recorded as a second source, NOT an independent third value). They exist here so the report can show, per row, that a BY-DESIGN divergence from Brandt is backed by a named physical source. NEVER backfill a unit-test expected value from these.

HT_span_ft._source: USAF 3-view; 18 ft 6 in. The PRIMARY HT span at L3 per Decision 1 (user, 2026-07-25) — area and span are what a 3-view measures, aspect ratio is definitional. +2.78% vs Brandt's derived sqrt(AR*S)=18.0.

VT_sweep_LE_deg._source: T.O. 1F-16A-1. +18.75% vs Brandt Main!H21 = 40 — the locked physical divergence, todo.md 2026-07-24 GeomL3 §2.

fuselage_length_ft._source: T.O. 1F-16A-1. +2.15% vs Brandt Main!B32 = 46.5 — the locked physical divergence, todo.md 2026-07-24 GeomL3 §3.

wing_airfoil._source: T.O. 1F-16A-1 Fig. 1-2 (wing root and tip) — corroborates Brandt Main!B22 '1404' -> t/c 0.04. Same figure as .aerodynamics.af_manual.airfoil.

wing_control_surface_area_ft2._source: T.O. 1F-16A-1 Fig. 1-2: flaperon 31.32 + LEF 36.71. NB does NOT match Brandt Main!F18 LE-flap S = 21.314 (todo.md 2026-07-21 Finding 5) — an independent T.O. figure, not a Brandt cell.

internet._note: ESTIMATE. Brandt's own textbook polar ('Introduction to Aeronautics: A Design Perspective') instead gives CD0=0.018 (CD=0.018+0.117*CL^2).

brandt._source: Brandt-F16-A.xls Miss!CD0_TO (readme_aero.md). Clean CD0 + gear/flap increment.
Brandt-F16-A.xls Miss!k1 (readme_aero.md). Quadratic / induced term (CD = CD0 + k1*CL^2 + k2*CL).

internet._source: 'Aerodynamic Performance Analysis of F-16C' (ResearchGate), quadratic coefficient.

brandt._source: Brandt-F16-A.xls Miss!k2 (computed, Aero!G17 = -2*k1*CL0). readme_aero.md. Linear / camber term.

internet._source: 'Aerodynamic Performance Analysis of F-16C' (ResearchGate), linear CL term of CD=0.01667+0.1167*CL^2-0.009*CL.

brandt._source: Brandt-F16-A.xls Miss!LD_max (readme_aero.md). Brandt simplified 0.5/sqrt(CD0*k1), ignoring k2, on the mission CD0=0.0270 basis.

internet._source: Brandt, 'Introduction to Aeronautics: A Design Perspective' textbook polar (CD=0.018+0.117*CL^2) -> LDmax=10.9.
internet._note: ESTIMATE; published clean subsonic L/Dmax band ~10.4-10.9. Higher than Brandt-workbook 8.93 because it uses the lower textbook CD0=0.018 vs the mission CD0=0.0270.

brandt._source: Brandt-F16-A.xls Miss!CL_opt = sqrt(CD0/k1) (readme_aero.md). CL at max L/D on the mission polar.

internet._source: Brandt textbook polar (CD=0.018+0.117*CL^2) -> CL at L/Dmax = 0.39.
internet._note: ESTIMATE; lower because it uses the textbook CD0=0.018.

brandt._source: Brandt-F16-A.xls Aero!G12 = max(0.4, 4.6*(1-0.033*AR^0.53)*cos(Lambda_LE)^0.1 - 3.3). readme_aero.md. Brandt's own Oswald formula (differs from Raymer Eq 12.48/12.49).

internet._note: ESTIMATE; F-16C ResearchGate polar gives e~0.91.

brandt._source: Brandt-F16-A.xls Aero!A19 = max(0.6, 2/(2-AR+sqrt(4+AR^2*(1+tan^2(Lambda_avg))))). readme_aero.md. Brandt's per-surface span-efficiency (distinct from e0).
Brandt-F16-A.xls Aero!A28 (same formula/value as e_wing, for the stabilator). readme_aero.md.

Brandt-F16-A.xls Aero!G3 = Cfe_tab*S_wet/S_ref (Aero-tab basis, Cfe_tab=0.0037). readme_aero.md. This is Brandt's pure skin-friction prediction (used by aero_at_mach), distinct from the Miss-tab CD0=0.0270 mission basis.
Brandt-F16-A.xls Aero!A12 = 1 - 0.065*(cos(Lambda_LE)*tc_pct)^0.6. readme_aero.md. Computed by Brandt's own formula, not a T.O. number (todo.md Finding D).
Brandt-F16-A.xls Aero!F9 = sec(Lambda_LE) = 1/cos(40deg). readme_aero.md. Above this Mach the wing LE is supersonic.
Brandt-F16-A.xls Aero!L31 = max(0, S_ref - outboard_strip - inboard_strip) = 300.0 - 51.49 - 103.77. readme_aero.md CLmax Step 2.
Brandt-F16-A.xls Aero!H25 = CLalpha_total[/deg]*alpha_stall = 0.06150*16. readme_aero.md CLmax Step 1.

brandt._source: Brandt-F16-A.xls Aero!H29 = min(CLmax_trim, CLmax_from_flaps) = min(1.537, 1.426). readme_aero.md CLmax Step 5.

internet._note: ESTIMATE ONLY -- same caveat as CLmax_takeoff (no conventional TE flaps).

weights._comment: F-16A Block 10/15 Brandt-workbook per-component weight OUTPUTS (Wt tab), for the weights deep-dive's later comparison-report script to check computed L1/L2/L3 toolbox output against. All values in lb. These are NOT toolbox inputs (see examples/F16A/f16a_L{1,2,3}.json .weights for those). Never backfill a unit-test expected value from anything here (the tests' 19,148 OEW self-referential trap is exactly why -- see _oew_note).
weights._source: VnV/BrandtF16A/readme_wt.md §5-§8 + GroundTruth/cell-map.md (Wt sheet) + VnV/BrandtF16A/BrandtWeight.m; corrections.xls figures per docs/weights_parameter_usage.md §4 (from baseline/F16Baseline.m corrected variant). W_TO basis = 31,377 lb (Wt!B3).
weights._method_note: Brandt's structural line-items use a psf x area model (Wt!C7:H7 coefficients: wing 6.75 / fuselage 5.0 / pitch 6.0 / VT 6.0 / nacelle 4.5 / strake 4.5 lbf/ft2) -- closest to the framework's L2 (Raymer Table 15.2 psf, DIFFERENT coefficients 9.0/4.8/4.0/5.3). The framework's L3 uses the Raymer §15.3.1 statistical build-up, which groups mass differently (no separate nacelle or strake line; LG split main/nose; systems as ~9 sub-items). Exact per-component agreement is NOT expected (documented ±20-40% scatter). Nacelles (Wt!G9), strakes (Wt!H9), armament support (Wt!B31), and lumped 'other structure' (Wt!B29) have NO direct framework analog.
weights._oew_note: TWO OEW figures. PRIMARY = official original Brandt Wt!B12 = 19,980.70 lb (comparison-report Expected column; agreed by readme_wt.md §8, cell-map.md:142, BrandtWeight.m, F16Baseline.m:93). ALTERNATE corrections_xls = 19,148.08 lb = corrections.xls Wt!B12 (Casey's revised-weight workbook, F16Baseline.m:136). The L1/L2/L3 unit tests assert 19,148 but MIS-cite it as 'Brandt Wt!B12'; per VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md 2026-07-24 §3b that 19,148 traces to corrections.xls, NOT the original Wt!B12. Re-citation is a Step-2c code edit; the corrections.xls file itself is not chased.
weights._oew_tier_note: SUPERSEDES the last sentence of _oew_note as to WHERE the 19,148 lives. Phase 4 LOCKED: the OEW-vs-Brandt agreement check LEAVES the unit tier entirely (an agreement check is not a unit test, per CLAUDE.md's two-tier rule) and becomes a row in the weights_brandt_comparison report, Expected = 19,980.70 (Wt!B12), Alt = 19,148.08 (corrections.xls Wt!B12). It is therefore no longer re-cited inside TestWeightsL{1,2,3}; it is removed from them. Spec: examples/F16A/F16WeightsL2.md §F/§G.4; docs/weights_parameter_usage.md §4.

This cell was the frozen literal 20681 on F16WeightsL3 -- a Brandt OUTPUT used as an input, which also froze the whole landing-gear group against W_TO (todo §P4-17). Report row: examples/F16A/F16WeightsL2.md §G.4b.
